questions: Preserve DIRECT without planning overhead; distinguish size from semantic coupling.
Measure request validation, explicit invocation and promotion of remaining outcomes.
decision: Keep DIRECT as a zero-orchestration fast path, with explicit risk/promotion signals and evaluated activation; do not add a classifier call.
code_observations: The entrypoint already distinguishes DIRECT, FINAL_PLAN and PRIMARY_PLAN. DIRECT is an early exit, not the removal of model-capability or optional validation safeguards.
requestctl and promotectl separate intake from promotion. The latter preserves completed outcomes so promotion need not manufacture retrospective TODOs.
implementation_steps: Extend the existing routing corpus with short high-risk changes, long repetitive logs, medium cohesive CRUDs, unrelated workstreams and nearly finished tasks under context pressure. Preserve explicit invocation behavior.
Represent a route decision with bounded reason codes, estimated working set and remaining outcomes. Do not persist a plan or load orchestration references on a negative implicit match.
Add a promotion regression that retains edits and completed tests while creating TODOs only for outstanding deliverables. Keep source evidence pointers rather than copied conversation history.
Keep exact lifecycle/configuration commands outside semantic routing. Document the optional validate-or-fix exit in one short pointer, not an eagerly loaded monitoring manual.
Record bounded reason codes only in the selected workflow; a rejected implicit match creates no plan, ledger or study files.
Evaluate activation false positives, false negatives, extra tokens, latency and final correctness on distinct held-out prompts.
Separate routing mode from capability tier so a small risky fix can stay DIRECT with a qualified implementation route.
proposed_acceptance_tests: A one-module feature touching seven files remains DIRECT and leaves no plan artifacts.
A short security-sensitive fix remains direct when cohesive, but its model floor is not lowered.
A promoted task includes only remaining outcomes and preserves the original worktree.
Measure entrypoint bytes, referenced files actually loaded and routing false-positive/false-negative cases against baseline.
A near-finished high-context task stays DIRECT without creating control files.
A tiny security-sensitive edit can select a strong worker without forcing an orchestration plan.
Promotion preserves changed files and validated outcomes and schedules only remaining work.

cost_model: Compare E[C]=C_select+P(false_positive)*C_unneeded_plan+P(false_negative)*C_recovery using measured task strata; include final validation quality as a constraint, not a weighted excuse for unsafe routing.
unverified: Natural-language route choice still needs host evaluation; passing string checks alone does not prove correct semantic routing.
Automatic skill selection is host/model-dependent; structural metadata tests cannot measure it. No new model-call experiment was conducted.
runtime_experiments: No authenticated provider invocation, live quota/cost benchmark, independent model review, or Windows runtime test was performed in this research revision.
previous_decision: Keep a small selective router; add measured near-miss and promotion contracts instead of a second classifier model.
revision_delta: The first report favored a lightweight router but did not price activation errors. The revision adds a false-positive/false-negative decision test and explicitly compares one qualified agent at lower effort with delegated execution. Length is not a proxy for risk or independence.
decision_analysis: The cheapest routing decision is often the one already available from the request and repository metadata. A separate paid classifier has a fixed per-request charge and can still misclassify a tiny security edit or a large repetitive log. Keep explicit invocation and exact lifecycle commands deterministic; let implicit activation require evidence of durable coordination value.

Use a two-stage contract: cheap selection from purpose, interruption risk and independence, followed only after selection by context preparation. A cohesive CRUD with several files should not pay a planning tax. Conversely, a two-line authorization change can need strong implementation capability without needing durable orchestration. These are separate dimensions.

The new evaluation must compare four complete outcomes: no orchestration, explicit-only, selective metadata routing, and a paid classifier. Count unrequested planning files as a false-positive side effect. Evaluate late promotion after useful work has already occurred; promotion must not restart accepted work.

Research supports testing simple alternatives, not assuming the smallest instruction file will select correctly. Keep a small negative/near-miss corpus and a separate held-out activation sample. Metadata lint and phrase-presence tests are necessary structural checks but cannot establish actual host selection behavior.
